title: Gather Victim Host Information: Firmware
summary: This sub-technique of Gather Victim Host Information narrows the focus from applications to firmware, the low level software stored on device chips such as basic input output systems, network switch images, router code and baseboard controllers. Firmware details are rarely exposed by ordinary network banners, so adversaries lean on elicitation, procurement paperwork, support forums and public tender documents where model numbers and revision levels are printed as a matter of routine. The intelligence value is inference: a firmware revision implies the hardware generation, its configuration, its purpose and how long it has gone unpatched, which in turn points at supply chain compromise or exploitation of an internet facing device. Telemetry is thin because nothing on the target network is necessarily touched, so detection usually depends on noticing collection attempts such as phishing messages that ask staff about device models, or on auditing which hardware details your organisation publishes. The distinction from the parent is scope rather than method, and defenders treat firmware inventory documents as sensitive.

beginner.definition: This is when an attacker collects details about the firmware on your devices. Firmware is the small permanent program built into hardware, such as a router or a printer. The attacker wants to know the model and version of that built in code.
beginner.whyItMatters: Firmware is often old and rarely updated, so it can hold serious weaknesses. A model number alone can tell an attacker how old your equipment is and how well you look after it. Because this collection usually involves no traffic to your network, it is very hard to spot.
howItWorks: The attacker gathers device model names and revision levels from your public support pages and manuals.
They read job adverts, purchase invoices and tender documents that list hardware you bought.
They may send phishing messages that ask a helpful member of staff which devices the office uses.
They match each model and revision against known firmware flaws and patch histories.
They use that match to judge which device is easiest to take over or to reach through a supplier.
Finally they plan an entry route, such as abusing an unpatched internet facing device.
beginner.example: Imagine a hospital that writes the make of every machine on a label beside each ward door. A visitor reads the labels in a corridor and later learns which of those machines has a known faulty lock. Nobody was harmed during the visit, yet the visitor now knows exactly which door to try.
takeaways: Firmware model and version details are valuable, so treat hardware inventory as sensitive.
Staff can be talked into revealing device details, so rehearse that question in awareness training.
Regular firmware updates remove the value of this reconnaissance over time.

objectives: Define host firmware and explain how it differs from ordinary installed software.
Explain why firmware version details let an attacker infer patch level and device purpose.
Describe how firmware information is elicited through phishing or open documents.
Recognise which of your own published materials may expose firmware detail.
Outline a firmware inventory and update routine that limits exposure.
